findings.text: Hypothesis h-02 is not supported. The mean gain is 2.092 dB at -10 dB but 8.994 dB at +10 dB, so the advantage is smallest, not largest, at the lowest SNR.
The LMMSE baseline is a scalar Wiener shrinkage, not a full-covariance LMMSE. A full-covariance baseline would narrow the reported gap.
All three low-SNR intervals exclude zero, and the exact sign-flip permutation p-values remain below 1e-04 after Holm correction across the three registered points.

uncertainty: Per-seed variability is the dominant source of spread at every SNR point.
The bootstrap is a percentile bootstrap over 20 paired differences; coverage at n=20 is approximate. The p-values are exact enumerations and carry no such caveat.
limitations: Synthetic exponentially decaying Rayleigh channels only; no measured channels.
The baseline is scalar-Wiener LMMSE, which is weaker than full-covariance LMMSE.
Claim c-03 concerns the trend direction across SNR and is stated only for the grid points that were run.
The estimator labelled learned is a tuned delay-domain filter, not a trained neural network; the result bounds the structure, not the architecture.
recommendations: Add a full-covariance LMMSE baseline before claiming a general advantage.
Extend the SNR grid below -10 dB to locate where the gain collapses.
